text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed mostly higher in quiet dealings. Near October ended $1.20 down at $325.0 per tonne, while December added 10 cents to close at $321.9 per tonne. The first German sugar beet test confirms that production in Germany may be down on last year. The first test showed a sugar yield of 3.93 tonnes per ha compared with 4.01 tonnes in the first test of 1996/97. This, together with a slightly lower sugar beet area means, that production will most likely be down on last year's 4.2 million tonnes, white value.

Raw sugar futures in New York remained almost unchanged. October added 3 points to close at 11.61 cents/lb, while March remained unchanged at 11.77 cents/lb. Brazilian producers are believed to be consistent hedge sellers since the practical removal of export quotas. News of a lower Thai crop failed to stir the market as this was already built into prices.

GERMANY ** - The first sugar beet tests for Germany show that the results are not as promising as last year but there is still potential for the crop to improve. Sugar content on August 1 reached 12.6 per cent, down from 13.9 per cent in 1996 and also well below the five-year average (1992/96) of 14.3 per cent. At 31 tonnes per ha root yield is slightly above last year's 28.8 tonnes but below the five-year average of 32.4 tonnes. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 3.9 tonnes, white value, slightly below the 4 tonnes of 1996 and also below the average 4.6 tonnes. However, a rather high weight of foliage of 650 grams per root (1996: 598 grams) as well as a high number of roots per ha of 83,000 units compared to 83,600 units in 1996, but well above the average of 80,440 units suggest that the crop has still good potential to develop favourably.

UKRAINE ** - Sugar exports in June 1997 amounted to 54,130 tonnes, raw value, down from 91,185 tonnes exported in May 1997. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1997 up to 517,718 tonnes. Major countries of destination in 1997 were Russia with 340,699 tonnes whites, Belarus with 47,700 tonnes, Aserbaijan with 19,199 tonnes and Turkmenistan with 16,600 tonnes.

Given expectations of an overall sugar production of 2.9 million tonnes (2.35 million tonnes from domestic beet) this year and domestic consumption of around 1.95 million tonnes, Ukraine will be able to export around 1.2 million tonnes, white value, sharply down from the previous year's 1.6 million tonnes.

CANADA ** - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 57,748 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from 166,746 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first eights months of 1996/97 (October/May) up to 687,008 tonnes against 830,629 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.160 million tonnes against 1.013 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Australia with 502,737 tonnes raws against 494,229 tonnes, Cuba with 59,520 tonnes, down from 117,743 tonnes and Brazil with 53,578 tonnes, up from 24,500 tonnes.
